reasoning.text: The render reads cleanly as an FPGA NTT card: ISO shows the open butterfly frame with all eight copper multiplier cylinders and the symmetric add/sub pairs exposed from above, the blue BRAM bank stack on the left edge, the exploded lane and exploded heatsink lifted clear so nothing is swallowed, and FRONT/SIDE confirm parts sit on the board with the twiddle/read/return buses standoff-grounded (no floaters). The real failure was never geometry — it was that the carried reproducibility findings showed the scene's annotations could not let an engineer rebuild the datapath: no primitive root, no radix-4 butterfly equations or 3-twiddle assignment, no per-stage crossbar permutation, no FSM transition table/loop bounds, no per-bank BRAM addressing beyond bank 0, and an abstract host boundary with no protocol. I addressed those by recording concrete reproduction values into the named part specs without touching metadata.spec/info. Remaining shortfall is that a static scene cannot realize the paper's *concurrent* 9-cycle pipeline / true per-stage crossbar routing — it is documented, not structurally enacted.
gaps: Architecture realization: the 9-cycle lane pipeline, the eight concurrent lanes, and the crossbar are documented in specs but not enacted as timed/concurrent structure — a static scene cannot show the per-cycle dataflow; pipeline cycle counts remain reproduction defaults, not the paper's reported figures

The radix-4 datapath is still modeled as eight radix-2 lanes with a config selector describing the fusion, rather than four physically distinct fused radix-4 BUs — consider modeling lane-pairs as merged 4-input units to make the headline contribution visible in geometry

Crossbar permutation is recorded as a reproduction rotation sigma_s; the paper's exact Sec. III bank-index/offset functions are still not transcribed (source does not give them) — flag as reproduction-chosen, not source-exact

Transform flavor and primitive root are now concrete in twiddle_rom but metadata.spec still labels the flavor 'implied'; an amend pass should reconcile metadata.spec.params.transform_flavor with the negacyclic psi=1945 recorded at part level
Geometry headroom: the central return/read buses crowd the lane-3/4 gap in TOP; a slight +Y lift or thinner profile would further separate the read/twiddle/return triad for the X-ray test

params.dma: scatter-gather; one polynomial = N=1024 x 14-bit coefficients packed little-endian into 64-bit beats (~4.57 beats per 8-coeff group)
params.framing: per-transfer descriptor {base_addr, length=1024 words, dir(in|out)}; one descriptor per polynomial vector
params.fifo_handshake: AXI-Stream style ready/valid into input_fifo and out of output_fifo; deasserted ready back-pressures and stalls the DMA engine
params.ordering: coefficients streamed in natural index order i=0..1023; transformed results drained in natural order (no bit-reversal pass)

after.notes: Reproduction I/O protocol. The source models this boundary abstractly as in-memory coefficient vectors with no protocol/ordering semantics; the widths, framing and handshake recorded here make the host edge rebuildable by a CS student.

params.addressing: identical map to every bank: a coefficient with global index i lives in bank b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 at offset o(i)=i>>3; bank 1 holds exactly the indices whose b(i)=1
params.capacity: 256 words x 14 bits ~= 3.5 Kb sub-region of an 18 Kb BRAM primitive

after.notes: Banks 1-7 replicate bank 0's word/depth semantics; only the resident index set differs (the b(i)=k preimage). 8 banks x 256 words = 2048 >= N=1024, leaving double-buffer headroom for ping-pong between forward and inverse passes.

before.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map satisfies the asserted no-conflict property and is rebuildable by a CS student.

params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle

after.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.

params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^k 2N-th-root pre/post-twist factors for the negacyclic case
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block

before.notes: Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction stores psi powers; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but does not give the table contents or primitive root.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 8857
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

after.notes: Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction stores psi powers with the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints.

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle

before.notes: Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs radix-2; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing.

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle
params.radix2_butterfly: Cooley-Tukey: with w=omega^k, u=x0, v=w*x1 -> y0=(u+v) mod q, y1=(u-v) mod q
params.twiddles_per_radix4_BU: 3 nontrivial twiddles W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3 (so 3 modular mults); j=psi^512 is a stored constant rotator, not a fetched twiddle
params.op_counts: radix-4 BU = 3 modular mults + 8 modular add/sub, vs two radix-2 stages = 4 mults + 8 add/sub on the same 4 points; the paper's rearranged schedule realizes 33% fewer modular multiplications and 20% fewer modular add/sub overall

after.notes: Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs radix-2; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing. The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings.

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
before.notes: The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. Exact state-transition table and loop bounds are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property.

transitions: LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

loop_bounds.stages_radix4: S4 = log4(N) = 5 passes, each fusing two radix-2 stages
loop_bounds.blocks_per_stage: N / 2^(s+1) groups at stage s, each sharing one twiddle factor

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
